content.thinking:
The real impact was latency rather than errors, since the error rate stayed flat versus baseline — meaning no extra requests failed during the six-minute incident, which was resolved via a config rollback. I'm noting that the cache endpoint port change is only inferred from deploy timing and connection-refused logs rather than confirmed directly, and treating the ClientDisconnected errors as unrelated background noise while I look at the latency spike from roughly 26ms to 190ms.

Rollback confirmation rests on a single check, and I never actually tested the alternative hypotheses like a code change or Redis outage. I should keep the exec summary free of impact figures and component names.

assumptions: The impact was latency only: the error rate during the window matched the pre-incident baseline, so no requests are believed to have failed that otherwise would have succeeded.

The causal link between the deploy and the cache failures is inferred from timing (the first connection-refused log coincides exactly with the release) plus the refused-connection messages naming the changed endpoint; nobody independently verified that nothing was listening on port 6380.

Two alternative explanations were raised and never tested, because the configuration rollback resolved the symptom: that the release shipped changed code rather than only configuration, and that the Redis cache independently stopped listening at the same moment.

The recurring 'account page request failed - ClientDisconnected' errors were present for at least the half hour before onset and are treated as pre-existing background noise unrelated to this incident.
Recovery was judged from a single healthy check at 23:50:05Z, about 30 seconds after the rollback; no longer soak period was observed before the incident was closed.
The latency and cache-hit-ratio figures in the root cause come from the investigating agent's reading of the per-minute metrics and were not re-derived here.
The feature-flag provider showed no recent changes, so flag configuration was ruled out as a contributor.
input.executive_summary: For roughly six minutes late on 22 September, the shop's account pages were noticeably slower than usual. A configuration change released at the start of that window pointed the service at the wrong address for its fast-lookup data store, so every such lookup was refused and each page request had to be assembled the slow way instead. Pages still loaded and the share of failed requests did not rise above its normal level, so the effect on shoppers was slowness rather than errors or lost functionality. The automated responder was alerted about five minutes in, identified the change as the cause, reverted the configuration, and confirmed performance was back to normal within about a minute of starting to act. A draft code change has been opened for follow-up so the wrong address cannot be shipped again.
input.root_cause: A deploy to io-shop at 23:44:00Z changed the summary-cache endpoint to redis://cache.io-shop.svc.cluster.local:6380, a port with no listener, so every cache lookup was refused; the cache hit ratio fell to zero and requests fell through to the slow uncached path, driving p50 latency up and tripping the HighLatency alert. Rolling the configuration back restored the working endpoint and latency returned to baseline.
